Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right lower lung, to the later image (Figure 4), there is a clear increase in the density and extent of the right-sided opacity along with the development of new opacities in the left lung. This pattern of progressive, multifocal airspace disease that mimics pneumonia but persists or worsens over time is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma).
